title: Adaptive slot reclamation and queue triage playbook for hosted GPU capacity exhaustion
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity surge on 2025-02-12 we observed prolonged GPU pool starvation driven by long-running prefetched requests and optimistic admission from newly primed tenants. Queue depth grew non-linearly and autoscaler hysteresis delayed capacity reclamation, resulting in high tail latency and client throttling. This ticket captures the post-incident plan to (1) add an adaptive slot reclamation mechanism that reclaims in-flight admission credits from low-progress work, (2) implement a deterministic queue triage that orders eviction based on progress and tenant fairness score, and (3) improve telemetry and probes to detect impending saturation earlier.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: combination of (A) aggressive optimistic admission policy for warm/primed tenants, (B) lack of in-flight progress metrics for admission tokens, and (C) autoscaler hysteresis that prevented timely scale-out/scale-in. Impact: 18 minutes of elevated 95/99th latency for hosted text-generation endpoints and ~6% error-rate spike for medium-priority tenants. Recovery: manual admission scaling and temporary global soft-throttle at 2025-02-12T03:46. Lessons: admission must be coupled to measurable forward progress and pool controls should reclaim budget from stuck or low-progress work before enqueue growth compounds.
decisions: Implement adaptive slot reclamation: each admission credit will be attached to periodic progress heartbeats; lack of progress past a soft-threshold triggers reclamation and a best-effort retry path.

Queue triage ordering: eviction preference will combine (1) tenant fairness score, (2) request progress percentage, and (3) request age — this avoids punishing long-running but high-progress requests.

Soft-eviction vs hard-eviction: adopt best-effort soft evictions (graceful preemption + client-level retry hints) by default; reserve hard-evictions for pool-critical emergencies with explicit operator consent.
Introduce an async admission probe: background probes to estimate warm pool capacity and prime workers proactively in slow growth windows.
Telemetry-first rollout: expose per-tenant admission tokens, progress rate, and queue-pressure signals in Console before enabling automated reclamation.
Keep autoscaler hysteresis tuning conservative: shorten downscale windows but cap aggressive upscales until reclamation proves stable.
Rollout strategy: feature-flag the reclamation and triage logic with canary % and staged enablement by tenant tiers.
action_items: ENG-668312-A1: Add per-admission progress heartbeat (Marco Diaz) — 3 points — deliver patch to runtime agent to emit progress every 200ms.
ENG-668312-A2: Implement reclamation controller that revokes idle admission credits and returns a 429-with-retry-hint (Priya Nair) — 5 points — guarded behind feature flag.
ENG-668312-A3: Build queue triage comparator in scheduler and test with synthetic load (Alex Chen) — 3 points.
ENG-668312-A4: Dashboard and alerting: queue depth + token age heatmap + reclaimed token counter (Observability) — 2 points — link to dashboard in links.
ENG-668312-A5: Autoscaler policy tweak PR and canary runbook (Triage Runbook) (SRE Team) — 2 points — include rollback criteria.
ENG-668312-A6: Customer communication template for tenants affected by soft-eviction policy (Customer Ops) — 1 point.
ENG-668312-A7: Post-rollout monitoring window (72 hours) and quality gate: <5% retry surface increase and no P99 increase >10% (All) — ongoing.
Follow-up: schedule cross-team run (Product + SRE + Runtime) to simulate cascade scenarios once reclamation is live.
timeline_highlights: 2025-02-12T03:10: incident begins — rapid increase in enqueue rate for hosted-text-gen v2 on pool-west-1.
2025-02-12T03:22: observed queue doubling every 3 minutes; alerts for queue-depth FRACTIONAL_THRESHOLD triggered.
2025-02-12T03:33: autoscaler attempted scale-out but delayed due to downscale window lock; manual override requested.
2025-02-12T03:46: applied global soft-throttle to reduce new admissions and stabilize latency.
2025-02-12T03:58: pool stabilized after admission throttles and operator-initiated scaling; incident closed at 2025-02-12T04:05.
2025-02-14: initial postmortem draft and stakeholder review completed.
notes: Prototype observations: reclamation reduces effective queue depth by ~30% in local sim but introduces ~2% retry surface when preemption hits long-tail requests.
Need UX/SDK hints to propagate retry-backoff metadata to clients so retries are less aggressive.
Consider a future enhancement: admission token weighting by expected cost (tokens cost proportional to estimated token-generation length).
Coordinate with Product for tenant opt-out window for conservative customers who prefer no soft-evictions.
Ops: add a one-click operator button to drain reclaimed tokens and surface reclaimed-token diagnostics in console.
